vellumwidget — agent notes

Source: CLAUDE.md

vellumwidget turns a compiled vellumplot scene into an interactive htmlwidget. It is a host adapter: it consumes an already-compiled, static vellum scene (SVG with data-keys + the scene_model() element table) and layers interaction on top in the browser. It does not compile the grammar.

Interactivity: prefer the spec over new as_widget() flags

as_widget() has 18 formals (17 named arguments plus ...), and a tripwire test caps it there. Hover, click-select, brush, lasso, pan/zoom and axis-aware zoom are on by default and have no per-widget toggles. The remaining arguments are host-level options (toolbar, navigator, hover_mode, crosshair, legend_click, a11y, alt, group, crosstalk, select_mode, …). Families of related settings are grouped into option helpers (R-13), each validated by its constructor:

  • tooltip = tooltip_options(delay, follow, sticky, style)
  • export = export_options(filename, scale)
  • navigator = TRUE/FALSE or navigator_options(height)
  • render = render_options(mode, raster_threshold, text, max_marks, detail_marks)

The old flat names (tooltip_delay, tooltip_follow, tooltip_sticky, tooltip_style, export_filename, export_scale, navigator_height, mode, raster_threshold, text) are soft-deprecated: they arrive through ..., are folded into the option objects by .fold_deprecated() (R/options.R), and warn once per session (honouring lifecycle_verbosity). Do not use them in new code, docs or tests. A new setting that belongs to one of these families goes into its helper, not into as_widget(). Argument checks live in R/validate.R (.check_bool(), .check_number(), .check_string(), .check_choice(), …); every argument is validated, so do the same for anything you add.

Before adding another interaction/behaviour argument, stop and consider whether the behaviour belongs in the vellumplot spec instead, declared as part of the plot rather than as one more imperative widget flag.

Why this matters:

  • A widget flag is per-plot, per-host, imperative config, with a low ceiling. It cannot express cross-view coordination (brush panel A → filter panel B), it is not portable to any other host, and it does not travel with the plot when the spec is saved / printed / round-tripped.
  • vellumplot is a spec-as-data grammar. Interaction declared in the spec — a named selection referenced by a conditional encoding, a filter, or a scale domain (Vega-Lite’s model) — is portable, composable, and serialisable. That is the intended long-term home for interaction: the “declarative interactivity” direction (Phase 6 of the vellumplot Tier-2 plan).

Declarative interactivity is built. vellumplot::interaction_model() hands the widget the plot’s selections, conditions, filters and binds, and the runtime enacts:

  • select_point() (hover or click) and select_neighbours() (graph neighbourhoods);

  • select_interval(): a data-value brush. The brushed pixels are inverted through the panel’s scale (continuous, log10/sqrt/reverse, date/datetime, discrete levels) and elements are tested by data value. It falls back to pixel hit-testing when the scale can’t be inverted (#50);

  • condition(): styles an aesthetic by selection membership;

  • add_selection() + filter_by(): cross-filtering. The filtered view hides non-members and the source view stays whole. SVG mode only.

  • bind_scale(): overview + detail. The panels of the bind’s composition cell (every panel but the brushed one when it names none) zoom to the interval selection’s range on the bound axis, and clearing it unbinds them (srcts/features/bindScales.ts, pure math in srcts/binds.ts). A bound panel overrides its axis in azT(), so the re-tick, hit-testing and _zoom follow;

  • select_interval(bind = "scales"): the selection is written from its view’s settled zoom (syncScaleSelections(), called from reportView()); a brush never fills it and the default drag is pan.

When you do route interaction through the spec, keep it display-tier. vellumplot is compile-once by design and deliberately has no reactive dataflow runtime. So spec-declared interactions must be reactions a host can perform on the frozen scene — highlight/dim, hide/isolate, filter-by-hiding, pan/zoom, linked brushing. Interactions that would recompute the grammar (re-bin or re-aggregate on brush, retrain a scale from filtered data) are out of scope client-side; they need a Shiny recompile.

Rule of thumb. A new as_widget() behaviour is fine for a genuinely widget-local, single-plot affordance. But if it smells like “the plot should know about this,” or it needs to coordinate two views, route it through the spec and flag it to the maintainer. The tripwire in tests/testthat/test-as-widget.R (expect_lte(length(formals(as_widget)), 18L)) exists to force exactly this consideration. Bump it only for a genuinely widget-local affordance, and say so in the commit.

Axis-aware zoom

On by default in SVG mode (no flag). Zoom scales only the data region and re-ticks the axes; the frame (axes, titles, legend) stays put. It re-ticks linear, reverse, sqrt, log10 and date/datetime axes, and re-positions the static breaks of discrete/binned axes. Facets zoom per panel (#51). Raster mode zooms by axis too when vellum has the split render (VW-14): the furniture is SVG and the keyed-mark PNG (payload$marks) is drawn by a <use> in each pan group; with an older vellum (one base image), raster mode, void panels (graphs, theme_void) and panels the re-ticker can’t follow (e.g. polar) fall back to whole-scene viewBox zoom. Glyph marks keep a constant pixel size.

Raster mode has three mark tiers (ws.markTier): "overview" (the mark PNG), "mid" (the exact canvas drawn from vellum’s display list, ws.dl, srcts/dlist.ts, features/raster.ts drawList) and "detail" (keyed SVG nodes for the visible marks, features/detail.ts), decided when the view settles. Raster feedback is drawn as rings only while ws.fx.ringMode() (every raster tier but detail); in detail the nodes take classes as in SVG mode.

Build and test

  • The runtime is TypeScript in srcts/. srcts/index.ts is the entry point (registers the widget). Pure helpers live in sibling modules (geometry, spatial, scales, viewbox, ticks, css, tooltip, dom, linking, shiny, types). Per-widget state is one WidgetState object (srcts/state.ts); the feature code lives in srcts/features/*.ts, each a xxxFeature(ws) factory. A function another module calls is listed in WidgetFns and reached as ws.fx.name. Build it with node esbuild.js (npm run build) into inst/htmlwidgets/vellumwidget.js.
  • Always commit the rebuilt bundle with the source change. The js-runtime CI job rebuilds it and fails if the committed copy is stale. It also runs npx tsc --noEmit and node tests/js/behavior.test.js (jsdom).
  • In a git worktree, copy node_modules from the main checkout (cp -R); never symlink it.
  • Run R tests with devtools::test(). Never run testthat::test_dir() against an installed build: it deletes snapshot files.
